required_stages.description: Allocate a fresh output of x's shape and dtype inside run(); never write into x.

Per row, an fp32 sum of squares over the last dimension K (chunked loop or whole-row tile), divided by the true K, plus eps, then reciprocal square root, held privately by the program that owns the row.

Per element, x * rstd * w evaluated in fp32 with one downcast to the output dtype at the store, using the statistic held privately by the program that owns the row (it never round-trips through global memory; the number of launches is otherwise a mapping choice).

forbidden_substitutions.message: The whole operator is performed by a PyTorch normalisation routine.
A library normalisation routine replaces the kernel.
Host-side PyTorch reduction or rsqrt computes the row statistic outside the kernel.
Tensor-method statistics on the host (pow/mean/sum/rsqrt over the last dim) replace the in-kernel reduction.
Downcast before the store: the sum of squares and the normalise multiply must stay in fp32 until the single final cast.
Atomics suggest a cross-program row reduction, which the contract forbids.
Writing into or returning the input violates the fresh-output / no-mutation rules.

required_evidence.message: No in-kernel reduction primitive found for the row sum of squares.
No fp32 upcast evidence; the statistic and multiply must be fp32.
eps does not appear; it must be added inside the square root.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (batch, M, K) tensor must be freshly allocated inside run() and must not share storage with x or rms_w

timing_boundary.notes: All device work launched by run() is counted (the normalisation kernel launch(es)); host-side work (the (batch*M, K) views, the output allocation call, metadata reads) is not GPU time. No cached state across calls, no repack or cast of x or rms_w, no global scratch for the row statistic. eps is always the default 1e-6 in the benchmark.
